resources.string: Select a game to view disc and RAWG metadata.
Resume or return to X-OG Mobile?

X-OG Mobile is an experimental original Xbox emulator for Android. This build is still a proof of concept, but it is fully usable for basic gaming with video output, physical controller input, audio playback, game library scanning, and app-private system file setup. The emulation core is based on xemu master commit 92407546f45c from 2026-06-21.
Tap a control to select. Long-press to add more. Drag to move.
Halo 2 profile applied: Vulkan, skip boot animation, touch-look and gyro aiming.
Aim by dragging on the right side of the screen
Auto-import system files from a folder
Put your MCPX (512 bytes), BIOS (256 KB or 1 MB) and HDD image (.qcow2/.img) in one folder, e.g. Download/Xbox, then pick that folder.
Pick the folder that holds your MCPX, BIOS and HDD files (Android does not allow picking Download itself; use a sub-folder such as Download/Xbox).
Scanning folder for MCPX, BIOS and HDD...
System files ready. You can start a game.
Some files are missing; add them to the folder or pick them manually below.

The emulator core stopped with a fatal error (the app stayed open). Reason and last core messages below. Fix the cause, then close the app completely and reopen it before trying again. You can send this with Settings → Share emulator log.
Last time the emulator crashed while running. Last core messages below (Settings → Share emulator log to send them).
MCPX must be exactly 512 bytes (yours: %1$d). xemu closes immediately with a wrong MCPX. Re-import it.
Warning: MCPX checksum %1$s does not match a known MCPX 1.0/1.1 dump; it may be corrupt.
BIOS must be 256 KB, 512 KB or 1 MB (yours: %1$d bytes). Re-import it.
The HDD file is not a qcow2 image or is too small. Use xbox_hdd.qcow2 from the xemu project.
Full (Redump) disc image detected: the emulator will read its game partition directly (no conversion needed).
Warning: no Xbox file system found in the game image. It may be corrupt or not an Xbox disc. Trying anyway…
Mali GPU diagnostics (applied on next Play)
Fast path: no geometry shader for triangles (depth less precise)
Safe buffer access (avoids GPU memory faults)
Disable occlusion queries (all objects reported visible)
Aggressive Mali mode: enables all options below and skips depth buffer sync (overrides them)
Full screen (fill the whole phone display)
Xbox widescreen 16:9 mode (games render wide, less stretching)
Widescreen will be applied from the next launch (the Xbox EEPROM is created on the first one).
Sharp textures (16x anisotropic filtering, more detail at the same resolution)
Present frames from the CPU (no Vulkan swapchain; avoids Mali GPU resets)
